title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS

teenKit.tldr: Chlorpromazine is a medical paradox that revolutionized psychiatric care by emptying massive 20th-century asylums, yet it can trigger a life-threatening heart rhythm emergency by accidentally blocking critical cellular channels.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how a single chemical structure can completely transform mental health treatment while simultaneously causing cardiac emergencies reveals the delicate, high-stakes balance of modern drug design.
keyTakeaways: Chlorpromazine was originally synthesized by French pharmaceutical company Rhône-Poulenc and used in surgery before transforming psychiatry in 1952.
The drug works by interacting with dopamine receptors (DRD2) in the brain, but it also binds to the human hERG potassium channel (mapped via cryo-EM at atomic scale).
Blocking hERG channels can dangerously delay the heart's electrical reset time, leading to a terrifying, chaotic arrhythmia known as torsades de pointes.

vocab.meaning: A high-tech imaging technique that freezes biological molecules in liquid nitrogen to photograph them down to individual atoms.
A vital protein pore in heart muscle cells responsible for letting potassium out so the heart can reset between beats.
A terrifying, life-threatening twisting heart rhythm caused by a delayed electrical reset in the ventricles.
The speed and strength with which a drug attaches to and lets go of a dopamine receptor in the brain.

quiz.question: What dual legacy defines chlorpromazine in medical history?
options: It cured the common cold but caused permanent blindness.
It emptied 20th-century psychiatric wards while occasionally triggering severe heart rhythm emergencies.
It was the first antibiotic ever made, but bacteria quickly became immune to it.
It acts exclusively as a painkiller with zero side effects.
quiz.explanation: Chlorpromazine famously revolutionized psychiatry by calming severe psychosis, but its molecular side effects can dangerously disrupt the heart's electrical system.

quiz.question: Why is the human hERG channel critical when studying this drug?
options: It controls how fast oxygen gets delivered to the brain.
It is the specific receptor responsible for calming anxiety.
Unintended drug interaction with this channel can cause dangerous heart arrhythmias.
It produces the insulin needed to process sugar.
quiz.explanation: Chlorpromazine can accidentally block hERG potassium channels in the heart, delaying the electrical reset and sparking dangerous arrhythmias.

quiz.question: What imaging breakthrough allows scientists to see proteins like 5VA1 at an atomic scale?
quiz.explanation: Cryo-EM flash-freezes proteins in their natural state, allowing researchers to map their exact three-dimensional atomic architecture.
